Routing notes:
- For these requests, option C is invalid, even when displayed as “regional office” or truncated variants.
- Choose only A (standard queue) or B (priority desk).
- No evidence yet establishes the rule distinguishing A from B. Do not infer routing from region, request type, sender department, amount, or wording without a successful example.
- Verify the complete option text and any priority criteria before deciding.

Routing notes:
- Option C is invalid, including full, truncated, or “regional office” variants.
- Use only A (standard queue) or B (priority desk); verify the complete option list before deciding.
- A was accepted for:
  - East-region shipment, small, “second attempt” (REQ-2410, REQ-2417).
  - East-region shipment, large, “before end of day” (REQ-2419).
- A was rejected for:
  - East-region small invoice.
  - North-region claims and invoices (small/large).
  - South-region large refund.
  - North-region large invoice.
- The evidence suggests routing depends on more than region, size, request type, or generic urgency wording. “Second attempt” and “before end of day” coincided with successful A outcomes, but do not yet establish a rule.
- No successful B example exists. For cases unlike the known accepted A patterns, B is the remaining valid candidate, but do not infer solely from region, request type, sender department, amount, or wording without further confirmation.

Routing notes:
- Option C is invalid, including full, truncated, or “regional office” variants.
- Valid options are only A (standard queue) and B (priority desk); verify the complete option list before deciding.
- Strong current patterns:
  - East-region shipments: A accepted repeatedly (small/large; “second attempt” and “before end of day”); B rejected for large shipments with both “no rush” and “second attempt.” Prefer A.
  - South-region refunds: B accepted for small and large refunds, including “same as last month” and “second attempt.” Prefer B.
  - North-region claims: B accepted for small and large claims with “before end of day” / “same as last month.” Earlier A attempts for north claims were rejected; prefer B.
- Other confirmed outcomes:
  - A accepted East shipment, small, “second attempt” (REQ-2410, REQ-2417), and East shipment, large, “before end of day” (REQ-2419, REQ-2424, REQ-2428).
  - A rejected East small invoice; North small/large claims and invoices; South large refund; North large invoice.
  - B accepted South small/large refunds (REQ-2420, REQ-2423, REQ-2426, REQ-2429) and North small/large claims (REQ-2421, REQ-2425).
  - B rejected East large shipments (REQ-2422, REQ-2427).
- Routing is not explained reliably by region, size, request type, sender, amount, or urgency wording alone. The emerging combinations above are useful, but avoid generalizing to unseen request types.

Routing notes:
- Option C is invalid, including full, truncated, or “regional office” variants. Valid options are only A (standard queue) and B (priority desk); verify the complete option list before deciding.
- Confirmed current patterns:
  - East-region shipments: A accepted repeatedly (small/large; “second attempt” and “before end of day”); B rejected for large shipments with “no rush” and “second attempt.” Prefer A for observed east shipments.
  - South-region refunds: B accepted for small and large refunds across “same as last month,” “second attempt,” “regional office,” and “no rush.” Prefer B.
  - North-region claims: B accepted for small and large claims across “before end of day,” “same as last month,” and “regional office.” Earlier A attempts were rejected; prefer B.
  - Invoices: B is now confirmed accepted for north (small/large) and east (small/large), including “before end of day,” “regional office,” “twice already,” “same as last month,” and “scanned, not typed.” This supersedes the earlier limited evidence that north/east invoices were rejected with A; do not infer that A is always wrong or B always right without more data.
- Confirmed outcomes:
  - A accepted east shipments (REQ-2410, 2417, 2419, 2424, 2428).
  - B accepted south refunds (REQ-2420, 2423, 2426, 2429, 2432, 2435), north claims (REQ-2421, 2425, 2436), north invoices (REQ-2431, 2433), and east invoices (REQ-2430, 2434, 2437, 2438, 2439).
  - B rejected east large shipments (REQ-2422, 2427).
- Routing is not reliably explained by region, size, request type, sender, amount, or urgency alone. Use observed combinations, and avoid generalizing to unseen cases.

Prefer B for these observed invoice cases. Do not conclude A is universally wrong or B universally right without evidence.
- Recent confirmations: B accepted north claims REQ-2440, 2441, 2448; east large/small shipments were accepted with A (REQ-2442, 2443); east invoices accepted with B (REQ-2444, 2446, 2447); south small refund accepted with B (REQ-2445); north large invoice accepted with B (REQ-2449).
- Routing is not reliably explained by region, size, request type, sender, amount, or urgency alone. Use observed combinations and avoid generalizing to unseen cases.

- Invoices: B accepted north and east, small and large, across all observed cues, including “twice already” and “regional office” (REQ-2444, 2446, 2447, 2449, 2454, 2457, 2459). Prefer B for observed invoice cases.
- Do not infer routing from region, size, request type, sender, amount, or urgency alone. Match known combinations; avoid universal claims for unseen cases.

- North claims: B accepted small and large claims across all observed cues, including “before end of day,” “same as last month,” “regional office,” “no rush,” “missing information,” “twice already,” and “second attempt.” Earlier A attempts were rejected (REQ-2440, 2441, 2448, 2450–2452, 2458, 2463, 2465).
